quote: To expect the unexpected shows a thoroughly modern intellect.
author: Oscar Wilde
riddleComment: He would have found you adequate.

quote: It is a truth universally acknowledged, that a single man in possession of a good fortune, must be in want of a wife.
author: Jane Austen
riddleComment: She was precise about everything. She would have been precise about this.

quote: It was the best of times, it was the worst of times, it was the age of wisdom, it was the age of foolishness.
author: Charles Dickens
riddleComment: He wrote very long books. This is one sentence.

quote: All happy families are alike; each unhappy family is unhappy in its own way.
author: Leo Tolstoy
riddleComment: He wrote longer books than Dickens. He had opinions about farming.

quote: So we beat on, boats against the current, borne back ceaselessly into the past.
author: F. Scott Fitzgerald
riddleComment: He wrote this sentence last. He knew it.

quote: The world breaks everyone, and afterward, some are strong at the broken places.
author: Ernest Hemingway
riddleComment: He kept sentences short. Except this one.

quote: In the depth of winter, I finally learned that within me there lay an invincible summer.
author: Albert Camus
riddleComment: He was French. He was not warm about it.

quote: Not all those who wander are lost.
author: J.R.R. Tolkien
riddleComment: He wrote this in a footnote. He had many footnotes.

quote: There is no greater agony than bearing an untold story inside you.
author: Maya Angelou
work: I Know Why the Caged Bird Sings
riddleComment: She knew the weight of words.

quote: We are all of us the walking wounded.
author: Dean Koontz
riddleComment: He writes quickly. He has not stopped.

quote: All the world's a stage, and all the men and women merely players.
author: William Shakespeare
riddleComment: He wrote this for a Wednesday matinee.

quote: Tell all the truth but tell it slant.
author: Emily Dickinson
work: Tell all the truth but tell it slant
riddleComment: She preferred the slant.

quote: A book must be the axe for the frozen sea within us.
author: Franz Kafka
riddleComment: He wrote this in a letter. He wrote many letters.

quote: Ever tried. Ever failed. No matter. Try again. Fail again. Fail better.
author: Samuel Beckett
riddleComment: He considered this optimistic.

quote: I took a deep breath and listened to the old brag of my heart: I am, I am, I am.
author: Sylvia Plath
riddleComment: She was listening carefully.

quote: Pain and suffering are always inevitable for a large intelligence and a deep heart.
author: Fyodor Dostoevsky
riddleComment: He found this comforting.

quote: You never know what worse luck your bad luck has saved you from.
author: Cormac McCarthy
riddleComment: He used no quotation marks. He had a reason.

quote: If you only read the books that everyone else is reading, you can only think what everyone else is thinking.
author: Haruki Murakami
riddleComment: He runs marathons. He has written about this at length.

quote: The only thing that makes life possible is permanent, intolerable uncertainty.
author: Ursula K. Le Guin
riddleComment: She built worlds. She had rules for them.

quote: Things fall apart; the centre cannot hold; mere anarchy is loosed upon the world.
author: W.B. Yeats
riddleComment: He was concerned about the falcon.

quote: Freeing yourself was one thing; claiming ownership of that freed self was another.
author: Toni Morrison
riddleComment: She knew the difference.

quote: A woman must have money and a room of her own if she is to write fiction.
author: Virginia Woolf
riddleComment: She had strong opinions about rooms.

quote: The secret of getting ahead is getting started.
author: Mark Twain
riddleComment: He was not surprised.

quote: He was still too young to know that the heart's memory eliminates the bad and magnifies the good.
author: Gabriel García Márquez
work: Love in the Time of Cholera
riddleComment: He was Colombian. He was not brief about it.

quote: Think you're escaping and run into yourself. Longest way round is the shortest way home.
author: James Joyce
riddleComment: He considered this straightforward.

quote: I am not afraid of storms, for I am learning how to sail my ship.
author: Louisa May Alcott
riddleComment: She wrote it in six weeks. She was not asked if she wanted to.
